what-an-llm-is-and-how-it-predicts-token.r: A team treated a model as a database of facts and was surprised when it produced a confident but wrong answer. Seeing it as a system that predicts likely next tokens made them add retrieval and checks for facts.
what-an-llm-is-and-how-it-predicts-token.x: Reason about what the model can and cannot know. Fluency is not accuracy, so design for verification, and keep a clear boundary between what the model generates and what your system guarantees.

tokens-context-windows-and-limits.r: A chat feature worked for short conversations and then failed after a few dozen messages because the history exceeded the context window. Summarising older messages and counting tokens before each call fixed it.
tokens-context-windows-and-limits.x: Context is a budget for cost, latency and quality. Count tokens, place important content carefully, trim deliberately and test with long inputs, since quality often drops well before the hard limit.

sampling-temperature-and-determinism.r: A test passed on one run and failed on the next because the model gave different wording each time. Lowering temperature and checking structure rather than exact text made tests stable.
sampling-temperature-and-determinism.x: Lower temperature reduces variation but does not guarantee identical output. Design tests around properties and schemas, and treat any model output as variable.

training-fine-tuning-and-where-knowledge.r: A support bot invented a refund policy that did not exist. Giving it the actual policy text at question time and telling it to answer only from that text removed the invention.
training-fine-tuning-and-where-knowledge.x: Knowledge comes from training data and from context you supply. Prefer retrieval for facts that change, consider fine-tuning for style or narrow tasks, and measure hallucination on your own questions.

calling-an-llm-api.r: An integration crashed whenever the provider returned a rate limit error. Handling errors with backoff and a clear fallback message kept the product working during busy periods.
calling-an-llm-api.x: Treat the API like any unreliable dependency: timeouts, retries with jitter, idempotency, rate limits, streaming handling and secret management. Log requests safely without leaking personal data.

cost-latency-and-caching.r: A prototype cost little in testing and a lot in production, because every request carried a large fixed prompt. Caching the shared prefix and trimming it cut the bill sharply.
cost-latency-and-caching.x: Cost scales with tokens, so estimate per request and per user before launch. Cache stable prefixes, route simple tasks to smaller models and watch latency from both input size and output length.

choosing-and-evaluating-models.r: A team picked a model from a public leaderboard and found it did worse on their own task. A small test set built from real examples showed which model fitted their needs and at what price.
choosing-and-evaluating-models.x: Evaluate on your data, with clear metrics and a fixed test set that you keep updating. Track quality, cost and latency together, and re-test when models change.

debugging-llm-applications.r: Users reported a bad answer. Capturing the exact prompt, retrieved documents and model settings showed that the retrieval step returned the wrong document, not that the model failed.
debugging-llm-applications.x: Log inputs, outputs and versions so you can replay a failure. Debug the pipeline stage by stage: retrieval, prompt, model, parsing, and fix the stage that is actually wrong.
